blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Delivering British-style customer service is about combining politeness with efficiency. Politeness without efficiency is hollow — the customer feels nicely spoken to while their problem is left unsolved. Efficiency without politeness is cold — the problem is fixed, but the customer feels processed rather than served.

At the Rise level, this means owning the problem in language and in action. "I'll take care of this personally and come back to you by end of day" is a sentence British customers love, because it promises both a person and a deadline. Then, crucially, you deliver on both.

When something goes wrong, apologise once, clearly, explain what you will do, and do it. British customers are forgiving of mistakes but very unforgiving of vague, evasive answers that feel designed to protect the company rather than solve the problem.

items.q: According to the text, why is politeness without efficiency described as "hollow"?
options: The company protects itself instead of the customer
The customer is spoken to nicely but the problem stays unsolved
The problem is fixed but the tone is cold
The customer is treated rudely and ignored
items.why: "the customer feels nicely spoken to while their problem is left unsolved" — som simpático, resultado zero.

items.q: What two things does the sentence "I'll take care of this personally and come back to you by end of day" promise?
options: A discount and an apology
A written report and a meeting
A person and a deadline
A manager and a refund
items.why: "it promises both a person and a deadline."

items.q: According to the text, when something goes wrong you should…
options: escalate the problem to a senior manager immediately
avoid admitting the mistake to protect the company
apologise repeatedly until the customer calms down
apologise once, clearly, explain what you will do, and do it
items.why: "apologise once, clearly, explain what you will do, and do it."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: British customers can forgive a genuine mistake.
A warm tone matters as much as a fast solution.
A polished, evasive answer is safer than admitting a fault.
Promising a deadline only works if you meet it.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que clientes britânicos são implacáveis com respostas evasivas — o contrário de 'mais seguro'.

items.q: What does the phrase "designed to protect the company rather than solve the problem" suggest about evasive answers?
options: They prioritise the company's comfort over the customer's need
They take longer to write than honest answers
They are only a problem in Britain
They are usually caused by poorly trained staff
items.why: Inferência: 'proteger a empresa em vez de resolver' revela a prioridade errada por trás da evasão.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry treinando o líder de equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, this account. The customer isn't angry because we made a mistake — they're angry because they feel politely ignored. Read the last three emails and you'll see it. Lots of warm words, "we appreciate your patience", "rest assured", and not one sentence that says who will do what, and by when.

That's the trap. We sound lovely and we solve nothing. To a British customer, that reads as evasive, and evasive is the one thing they won't forgive.

Here is what I want from you on the next call. Own it. Say "I'll look into this myself and come back to you by five o'clock today." A person and a deadline. Then, and this is the part that actually matters, you come back at five — even if it's just to say the case is still being reviewed. Silence after a promise is worse than the original problem.

And apologise once. Once, clearly, and then move straight to what happens next. If you keep apologising, it starts to sound hollow, and they stop believing you.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is the customer angry, according to Harry?
options: They were spoken to rudely on the phone
The company made a serious mistake
They were charged the wrong amount
They feel politely ignored rather than helped
items.why: "they're angry because they feel politely ignored."

items.q: What does Harry say is missing from the last three emails?
options: A sentence saying who will do what, and by when
The customer's account number
A clear apology
Warm and friendly language
items.why: "not one sentence that says who will do what, and by when."

items.q: According to Harry, what should you do at five o'clock even if the case is not finished?
options: Send a final apology and close the case
Come back to the customer anyway, even just to update them
Pass the case to a colleague
Wait until there is a full solution to report
items.why: "you come back at five — even if it's just to say the case is still being reviewed."

items.q: What does Harry mean by "Silence after a promise is worse than the original problem"?
options: Customers dislike phone calls more than emails
Promises should never be made to customers
The original problem is usually easy to fix
Breaking contact after committing damages trust more than the fault itself
items.why: Inferência: prometer e sumir corrói a confiança mais do que a falha inicial.

items.q: Why does Harry warn against apologising repeatedly?
options: It suggests the mistake was very serious
It wastes the customer's time on the call
It is against company policy
Repeated apologies start to sound hollow and lose credibility
items.why: Inferência: "it starts to sound hollow, and they stop believing you" — excesso de desculpas esvazia a mensagem.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A charming reply that solves nothing feels hollow to the customer." Hollow here means…
options: slow to arrive
empty — nice on the surface but with no real substance
aggressive and rude
highly detailed and technical
items.why: Hollow = vazio: soa bem, mas não entrega nada de concreto.

items.q: "He gave a vague, evasive answer that avoided the real question." Evasive means…
options: fast and efficient
clear and direct
designed to dodge the issue rather than address it
friendly and warm
items.why: Evasive = evasivo: foge do ponto em vez de encará-lo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We need to ___ this complaint — assign one owner who sees it through to the end."
options: postpone
process
own
forward
items.why: To own a problem = assumir o problema, ter um responsável claro do início ao fim.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "British customers are ___ of honest mistakes, but not of answers that dodge the point."
options: unforgiving
suspicious
unaware
forgiving
items.why: Forgiving = tolerante; o contraste é com evasão, que eles não perdoam.

items.q: "The problem was fixed, but she felt processed, not served." Feeling processed means…
options: being given a very fast solution
being treated as a case in a system rather than as a person
being transferred to another department
being asked to fill in a long form
items.why: Processed = processado: tratado como número/etapa, sem o cuidado pessoal.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns no atendimento ao cliente. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Leave it with me — I'll look into it and come back to you." To look into something means to…
options: investigate or examine it
ignore it for now
approve it formally
complain about it
items.why: Look into = investigar, apurar a questão antes de responder.

items.q: "We promised a fix by Friday, but nobody followed through." They…
options: asked another team to help
failed to carry the promise to completion
changed the deadline
apologised too many times
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi prometido.

items.q: "I'll get back to you by end of day with an update." To get back to someone means to…
options: refund their money
end the conversation
return their call or reply later as promised
transfer their case
items.why: Get back to = retornar o contato depois, dentro do prazo combinado.

items.q: "Don't brush off the complaint with a polite line — deal with it." To brush off means to…
options: dismiss it without taking it seriously
write it down in detail
handle it carefully
escalate it to a manager
items.why: Brush off = descartar, minimizar sem dar a devida atenção.

items.q: "The team lead offered to take ownership of the account." This means she agreed to…
options: delay any decision
buy the account from the client
review the paperwork only
accept full responsibility for resolving it
items.why: Take ownership of = assumir a responsabilidade completa por resolver algo.
